name: DecalProjector
src_typeComment: Drop on an empty GameObject positioned/rotated/scaled to define the decal's PROJECTION BOX — the object's local -Y axis is the projection direction ("down onto the surface"), local X/Z are the decal's footprint, and localScale sets the box size on all 3 axes (a Cube-primitive-style gizmo, drawn below, shows exactly where it will project) — then call Generate() (or use the "Generate Decal" context-menu entry) to spawn a real mesh clipped to whatever geometry sits inside the box.  Requires the receiving surface to carry BOTH a Collider (found via Physics.OverlapBox) AND a MeshFilter on the SAME GameObject (its triangles are what actually get clipped) — the normal "mesh + matching MeshCollider" setup most scene geometry already has.

src_serialized.name: surfaceMask
src_serialized.tooltip: Which colliders count as receiving surfaces for this decal.

src_serialized.name: decalMaterial
src_serialized.tooltip: Material applied to the generated decal mesh — needs a decal texture with alpha (a tire-mark or footprint shape, transparent elsewhere).

src_serialized.name: maxSurfaceAngle
src_serialized.tooltip: A source triangle whose normal points more than this many degrees away from the projection direction is skipped, so a floor decal doesn't wrap up onto a nearby wall.

src_serialized.name: surfaceOffset
src_serialized.tooltip: Small push outward along each vertex's own normal, avoiding z-fighting with the receiving geometry.
